data.long_meaning: Means 'present' or 'existent'. Derived from the Arabic root kh-b-r, which means 'to be present'. The name Khabiir carries the meaning “Present, Existent” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Khabiir usually hope their child will grow to embody present, existent and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khabiir total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: خبير
in_arabic.long_meaning: يؤتى هذا الاسم من جذر "خ-ب-ر"، ومعناه المستعد والذى له خبرة وذكاء، وهو من أسماء النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ويعد هذا الاسم من أسماء النجباء الذى له مستقبل ممتاز، ويكون هذا الاسم من أسماء الذى له حكمة وفهم، وفي بعض الأحيان يعبر الاسم عن الذى له خبرة كبيرة في شئ ما، وهو من أسماء الذى له مستقبل مشرق، ويعد هذا الاسم من أسماء الذى له شخصية قوية ومستقبل ممتاز.

in_urdu.name: خبیٰر
in_urdu.meaning: ذوخبرہ اور بڑھئے سے ہونے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: یہ نام جذر "خ-ب-ر" سے ماخوذ ہے، اور اس کا مطلب ہے کہ جو شخص ذہانت اور بصیرت کا مالک ہو، اور بڑھئے سے ہونے والا ہو، یہ نبی صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم کا نام ہے، اور یہ نام نجباء کا نام ہے جو مستقبل ممتاز رکھتا ہے، بعض اوقات اس نام سے وہ شخص کو کہا جاتا ہے جو کسی شے میں بہت سی معلومات رکھتا ہے، یہ نام نجباء کا نام ہے جو مستقبل روشنی والا ہے، اور یہ نام وہ شخص کا ہوتا ہے جو قوی شخصیت اور ممتاز مستقبل رکھتا ہے۔

historical_references.context: Khabiir ibn Al-Ashraf was a prominent poet and a fierce opponent of the early Muslim community in Mecca, particularly towards Prophet Muhammad. He mocked the Muslims and their faith, and was a major source of distress for them. Prophet Muhammad, while still in Mecca, sent Ali ibn Abi Talib to confront Khabiir and warn him of the consequences of his actions. Ali did so, and Khabiir responded by insulting Ali and the Prophet further. As a result of this, Prophet Muhammad put a curse on Khabiir, which ultimately led to his death by the hands of Ali when the Muslims, led by the Prophet, migrated to Medina.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Hisham's Sirah Ibn Hisham The name Khabiir carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Khabiir ibn Al-Ashraf was a prominent poet and a leader of the Quraysh, the ruling tribe of Mecca during the time of Prophet Muhammad. He was known for his eloquence and his vehement opposition to Islam. Prophet Muhammad, in response to Khabiir's insults and mockery of Islam, put a curse on him. Khabiir continued to mock the Prophet and the early Muslim community, but eventually, when the Muslims migrated to Medina, Khabiir was killed by Ali ibn Abi Talib in battle.
